newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish EU presidency gives priority to EU-US relations.
newsitem.headline: Irish EU presidency gives priority to EU-US relations.

text.p: The strengthening of EU-US relations is a significant priority for Ireland's EU presidency, Ireland said on Friday.
"The New Transatlantic Agenda (NTA) has an important part to play in enhancing EU-US cooperation in a variety of fields," Ireland's department of foreign affairs said in a statement.

It said the NTA reaffirmed the strong and enduring ties between the European Union and the United States and was the first step in a longer process of adapting the EU-US partnership to the new challenges it will face in the 21st century.

The NTA, which was signed in Madrid last December, was designed to strengthen the bilateral relations between the EU and U.S. and to enhance cooperation between the two sides in multilateral organisations, the statement said.

The four goals for the EU-US relationship include promoting peace, stability, development and democracy, responding to global challenges; contributing to the expansion of world trade; and closer economic ties and encouraging close communication between European and American business people, it said.
A new element of EU-US cooperation involves the creation of a high-level consultative mechanism to coordinate EU-US development and humanitarian assistance programmes, it added.
"Working together can improve our capacities to respond to humanitarian crises, promote development and support democracy and respect for human rights," Ireland said.
